//: Verification-only permission profile for Davinci agents. Grants exactly the commands agents need to prove their own work -- running tests, builds, lint, typecheck, and reading git/filesystem state. Deliberately excludes npm install, git commit, git push, and anything that deploys: agents do not need them to verify, and granting them widens the blast radius of a mistake. See README.md, 'Letting agents verify their own work', for how to apply this.
//shoot: The screenshot tool lives in the plugin directory, whose absolute path differs per installation, so it cannot be listed here. To let frontend-engineer see its own work, add: "Bash(node /absolute/path/to/davinci/scripts/shoot.mjs:*)". Without it the agent reports that visual verification was impossible rather than implying it looked.
//verification: Deliberately absent: node -e, node -p, and running an arbitrary script file. A builder is not bash-guarded by the write-scope hook (only read-only agents are), so this allowlist is the only thing standing between a builder and writing outside its scope through node fs. Granting node -e would remove the plugin's central safety property to save an agent one command. An assertion that needs real code belongs in a test run with node --test -- see "Proving something the allowlist will not run" in the delegation contract.
//generators: Discovery is granted (command -v) because a probe that cannot run reports an absent generator, which is a lie the page is then built on. Generation is not granted: it spends real credits, so the generating command is opt-in per project -- add e.g. Bash(higgsfield generate:*) and Bash(higgsfield workflow:*) alongside its account/model subcommands. Without them an agent finds the binary, correctly reports a blocked check, and still ships static -- honest, but not the outcome anyone wanted. An agent that finds a binary it may not run must report that as a blocked check, never as no generator.
//waste: The waste sweep lives in the plugin directory like the screenshot tool, so its absolute path differs per installation and cannot be listed here. To let builders see what their change orphaned, add: "Bash(node /absolute/path/to/davinci/scripts/waste.mjs:*)". It only reads. Without it an agent reports the sweep as unrun rather than reporting the project as clean.
//scaffold: Greenfield gap, found by measurement: npm run build/lint/test are granted above but need node_modules, and npm install is not granted -- so on an empty directory every verification command is inert and the agent cannot prove anything it wrote. This is deliberate. npm install runs a package's own postinstall scripts, which is arbitrary code execution and strictly worse than the node -e escape hatch refused above. To scaffold a new project, either run the generator yourself before dispatching (npx create-next-app, npm create astro, etc, then npm install), which is the recommended path, or opt in for that run by adding: "Bash(npm install)", "Bash(npm ci)", "Bash(npx --yes create-next-app:*)". An agent that finds these denied should hand-write the scaffold, mark it unverified, and say so -- never report it as built and working.
//seo: The SEO and markup check lives in the plugin directory like the other tools, so its absolute path differs per installation. Add: "Bash(node /absolute/path/to/davinci/scripts/seo.mjs:*)". It only reads, and it reads built output rather than source -- so it needs a build to have run. Without the grant an agent reports the check as unrun, never the page as fine.
//serving: Deliberately absent: npx serve, npx http-server, python -m http.server. A static server started by an agent outlives the screenshot that wanted it -- four were once found still running hours later, holding ports and a directory handle that blocked deleting the project. shoot.mjs --root <dir> <path> <out.png> serves the built output on an ephemeral port and stops it in a finally, so the case is covered without a grant that can leak. A dev server is refused for a different reason: it never exits, so it hangs the call that started it.
//checkpoint: The checkpoint tool lives in the plugin directory like the others, so its path differs per installation. Add: "Bash(node /absolute/path/to/davinci/scripts/checkpoint.mjs:*)". It writes only to .devteam/checkpoints/ and, on an explicit restore, to the working tree. It uses a shadow git repository, so the project's own history is never written to and no git commit grant is needed. Without it, slices are built with no way to take them back.
